A 4-year-old boy is brought to the pediatrician due to a low-grade fever. His mother reports that the
fever has been intermittent over the past 6 days, with temperatures ranging from 99.8°F (37.7°C) to
101.0°F (38.3°C), and that he experienced a similar episode three months ago. She also notes
symmetric swelling in his knees and wrists that has progressively worsened over the past 8 weeks. The
child has no cough, respiratory issues, or changes in bowel habits. He was born at 40 weeks gestation
and is in the 45th and 40th percentiles for height and weight, respectively. He is not on any
medications. His current temperature is 99.7°F (37.8°C), blood pressure is 104/84 mmHg, pulse is
106/min, and respirations are 14/min. Physical examination reveals a non-pruritic, macular,
salmon-colored rash on his trunk. Serological testing shows the following results: - Rheumatoid factor:
Negative - Anti-nuclear antibody: Negative - Anti-double stranded DNA: Negative - Anti-SSA: Negative
- Anti-SSB: Negative - Human leukocyte antigen B27: Positive - Erythrocyte sedimentation rate: 30
mm/h This patient is at greatest risk of developing which of the following? Answer Choices: (A)
Psoriatic arthritis (B) Enthesitis (C) Dactylitis (D) Chronic anterior uveitis (E) Spondylodiscitis (F)
Juvenile ankylosing spondylitis (G) Iridocyclitis (H) Sacroiliitis (I) Reactive arthritis (J) Aortitis
 A. Chronic anterior uveitis
B. Dactylitis
C. Spondylodiscitis
D. Iridocyclitis
E. Sacroiliitis
F. Reactive arthritis
G. Aortitis
H. Psoriatic arthritis
I. Enthesitis
J. Juvenile ankylosing spondylitis
